A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TrajVAD work, and their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains appendices; both reference separate supplementary material that is unavailable and cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v1 reports original TrajVAD experiments on ShanghaiTech, UBnormal and MSAD, including feature ablations, flow-depth analysis, computational measurements and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and additionally reports a simulated missed-detection experiment and an extended flow-depth sweep.

M1.justification: Equation 3 changes the documented coupling operation from v*exp(s(u))+t(u) to (v+t(u))*a(u), where a(u)=sigmoid(s(u)+2)+epsilon. This revises a method component while retaining the trajectory features, flow framework, pose conditioning and scoring objectives. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation or original runs changed.

E1.justification: The three datasets and their human-related subsets remain unchanged. v2 adds a ShanghaiTech test scenario with randomly missing detections, extending coverage to explicitly corrupted detection inputs.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 substantially broaden the supplied comparisons beyond pose and trajectory methods, adding 13 ShanghaiTech baseline rows and five UBnormal rows covering RGB, flow and multimodal approaches. Examples include MULDE, FPDM, BA-AED and SSMTL++. Table 7 also compares STG-NF and TSGAD under missed detections. v1 referenced broader comparisons in an unavailable supplement, so these are newly explicit comparisons in the supplied material, not established new baseline runs.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 changes the stated window length from T=16 throughout to T=12, 16 and 24 for UBnormal, ShanghaiTech and MSAD respectively. v2 also adds K=2 to the depth sweep and specifies random removal of 10% of detections per track. These are reported setting changes and additions; rerunning the original experiments is not established.

E4.justification: New Table 7 tests sensitivity to missed detections, supplementing the existing detector-quality discussion with a controlled corruption experiment. Figure 4 extends the depth analysis from K=6-22 to K=2-22. The feature-group ablation and qualitative cases are retained, although their presentation order changes.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new randomized detection-removal experiment also reports only point results.

E6.justification: Previously tabulated benchmark, timing and feature-ablation values are retained. Added results comprise the broader baseline rows, K=2 measurements and Table 7: TrajVAD-T drops from 84.9 to 82.4 AUROC, STG-NF from 85.9 to 80.7, and TSGAD from 80.6 to 76.1 under detection removal. These extend the evidence without demonstrating a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: Equation 3 revises the mathematical coupling map, introducing a sigmoid-based scale and applying translation before scaling. This is not equivalent notation. The remaining likelihood, gating and normalization equations are retained, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain multi-class bounding-box trajectories as a primary anomaly modality, eliminating mandatory pose estimation, and optionally adding reliability-gated pose information. Abstract and conclusion wording changes, but the principal performance and efficiency claims retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets Table 7 as evidence of stability under short detection gaps, particularly with smoothing, interpolation and track splitting. Section 5 explicitly adds missed detections and unstable track IDs as failure conditions. The earlier ShanghaiTech discussion connecting AP advantages to low-false-alarm deployment is removed; the main explanations of dataset-specific behavior remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly specifies Kalman smoothing, linear interpolation across gaps of at most 10 frames, and splitting at longer gaps. v1 only stated that coordinates were smoothed and deferred preprocessing details. These disclosures do not establish changed preprocessing. Conversely, v2 omits v1's explicit pose-weight value, lambda=1.0.

R1.justification: v2 adds seven cited works, including LSA, BA-AED, sRNN, CAE-SVM and VEC, and removes the CVPR 2021 self-supervised multi-task reference. Section 2.1 more carefully acknowledges spatial evidence from appearance methods while emphasizing persistent object-level cues. The central positioning around underused multi-class trajectories remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, appearance-based related work and conclusion are edited or rewritten, terminology and headings are standardized, and acknowledgements are added. Ablation and qualitative analysis exchange subsection order. The overall narrative structure and much of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 gain modality groups and additional rows; Table 7 is added and Table 6 is reformatted. Figure 2 revises the operation ordering and pose-branch drawing, while Figure 4 adds K=2 and changes axis ranges. Existing displays are relocated, with the overall visual format preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 provides better comparative context, explicit gap-handling instructions and a controlled detection-failure test supporting the robustness discussion. These are useful, limited improvements while headline numerical results remain unchanged. Reproducibility still has drawbacks: lambda=1.0 disappears, and Figure 2 places permutation before ActNorm while Section 3.3 still calls ActNorm the first transform.
